summary: Bug hunt under his standing brief (#690): four areas, real touch/mouse input, every finding a failing test; one skeptic per finding; a fixer per area

confirmed.title: In Select mode a finger swipe on the project list ticks projects instead of scrolling, so with a long library he cannot reach the projects further down
confirmed.see: He taps Select, or holds a card, to clear out his 60+ projects, then swipes up to get to the older ones. The list does not move at all. Every card his finger crosses gets a tick instead. The only thing that scrolls is the 16 px strip beside the cards, so the projects below the first screen cannot be reached to select them.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a in Select mode a finger swipe on his long project list ticks projects instead of scrolling it — he cannot get down to the rest. Fails at 380 and 900: with Select on and 63 projects, a real finger swiped 250 px up his list (the same swipe moves it 235 px with Select off) and the list moved 0 px, while 2 project(s) he only swiped across got ticked (Untitled, HUNTa7 swipe 1). Every swipe that starts on a card paints ticks instead of scrolling, so he cannot get down to the projects further down; only the thin strip beside the cards scrolls.
confirmed.evidence: styles.css:4748 `body.hm-selecting .hm-card { touch-action: none; }` gives every card gesture to the page. js/home.js:1699 `if (selectMode) { beginPaint(id, ev.clientY); }` starts a paint on every pointerdown in Select, and js/home.js:1735 turns any move over 8 px into painting. No path leaves a plain vertical swipe to the scroller.

Mouse drag-paint on PC can stay as it is.

verdict.reason:
This is a real problem, not a test artefact. I ran the test in the hunt7-a worktree at 380 px and it failed the same way the hunter reported. The control swipe, with Select off, moved the list 351 px. The same trusted CDP touch swipe with Select on moved it 0 px and ticked 2 projects he only swiped across ("Untitled", "HUNTa7 swipe 1"). The fixture is valid: the control shows the driver produces a real browser pan, and the swipe starts on a card, not on the select bar.

Code path:
- styles.css:4748 `body.hm-selecting .hm-card { touch-action: none; }` takes the pan away from the browser on every card.
- js/home.js selectify pointerdown: `if (selectMode) { beginPaint(id, ev.clientY); }`. Then any move over 8 px sets `paint.moved`, and paintTo ticks the span. Nothing sends a plain vertical swipe to .hm-scroll.
- While Select is on, the only ways to scroll by touch are the 16 px .hm-scroll padding, the 10 px gaps between cards (the hunter missed these, but it is a minor point), and the edge auto-scroll, which ticks everything it passes. Cancel clears the selection, so he cannot leave Select to scroll and come back.

Is it intended behaviour he asked for? Only partly. At v3.86 (POLISH-LOG line 160) he asked: "when you are selecting in the Home Screen you can do the drag thing that we have elsewhere to drag select a lot". The "elsewhere" is the timeline track heads. Even at v3.86 (dc75ab0d:js/timeline.js:463) those painted only after a 380 ms hold, and today a plain drag on a head pans the list. timeline.js:1429 records the same bug being fixed there: dragging did nothing, which "read as the layers don't scroll". Painting straight away while already in Select, with no scroll, was my own design choice in v3.86, not his words. REQUESTS.md has no entry asking to give up scrolling.

He would hit this: from 60 projects, Home shows "You have N projects. Tap Select to tidy up" (js/home.js:2367), which sends a big library into exactly this mode, and on a phone a swipe on the cards is how you scroll. Mouse and wheel on PC are not affected.

Whatever the fix is, it has to keep a drag-select path because he asked for one. The hunter's suggestion (hold, then paint, even in Select) matches the timeline gesture he pointed to.

confirmed.title: With 60+ projects, hold-and-slide ticks one more project than the finger passed over, because the list jumps 70 px when Select comes on
confirmed.see: With 60 or more projects, Home shows a note at the top of the list (You have N projects…). He holds a card to start Select, and the whole list jumps up 70 px under his finger. He slides down over two more cards and lifts on the third. A fourth project he never touched is ticked too, and the next Delete removes it as well.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a with 60 or more projects, holding a card and sliding over two more ticks a fourth project his finger never reached — the list jumps when Select comes on. Fails at 380 and 900: with 63 projects he held HUNTa7 hold 1 until Select came on, slid the same finger down over HUNTa7 hold 2 and lifted it on HUNTa7 hold 3. 1 more project his finger never reached got ticked too (HUNTa7 hold 4). When Select came on, the note left the top of the list and every card jumped 70 px up under his finger, so the slide ran a card further down the list than he did.
confirmed.evidence: js/home.js:2365 `if (h && h.level !== 'ok' && !selectMode) {` removes the health note as soon as Select is on. verdict.reason:
I ran the test twice and it failed both times, once in the default run and once in a 380 px window. Both runs reported the same thing: 63 projects, a 70 px jump, and HUNTa7 hold 4 ticked as well.

The code confirms the jump. This is not a quirk of the fixture or of the timing:

- **The note disappears when Select comes on.** With 60 or more projects, Home shows a "You have N projects" note (`FM.projects.health()` returns 'busy' at 60 or more). render() hides it while Select is on (js/home.js:2365, `!selectMode`). That condition came in with the original multi-select feature in v2.97. I found nothing in REQUESTS.md where he asked for it.
- **The hold rebuilds the list while his finger is still down.** When the hold fires (js/home.js:1707-1709), it turns Select on and calls render(), which empties the list and rebuilds it (`grid.innerHTML = ''` at 2324). Because the whole list is rebuilt, the browser's scroll anchoring cannot hold the cards in place. Every card moves up by the note's height plus the 10 px gap, about 70 px. The code's own comments say a rebuild must never move the card under his finger, and this one does.
- **The cards are 108 px tall.** That is the 86 px thumbnail plus padding and border, with a 10 px gap.
- **The hold turns sliding on straight away.** It marks the gesture as already moving, so any finger movement at all goes straight to paintTo(), which picks the card by where it sits on screen now.

The geometry makes the problem concrete. If he holds a card at its middle, after the jump his finger is 6 px inside the card below. The first slide movement, or even a small wobble while holding, ticks that next card, which he never held. Holding anywhere in roughly the lower two-thirds of a card does the same.

The report overstates one thing. The ticks redraw live on the moved cards, so a person watching the screen would see the fourth tick appear. It is not quite "a card his finger never reached". The real defect is the 70 px jump itself, and it moves the card he held out from under his finger. That breaks the hold-then-slide gesture that queue 690 made work, and a stray tick goes with the next Delete.

Scope: it only happens with 60 or more projects, since that is when the note shows. It happens at any scroll position, because the whole list is rebuilt. I'd call it medium rather than high: it is visible and can be undone by tapping the extra card, but it is still a real defect he would hit.

confirmed.title: Save project file… on another project from Home reloads the open project: its undo history, playhead and selection are lost, and the other card's picture is replaced with its first frame
confirmed.see: He is working in project A, goes Home and uses ⋯ → Save project file… on project B to back it up. When he goes back into A, Undo does nothing because his history is gone. The playhead has jumped back to 0 and his selected layer is no longer selected. B's card, which he only backed up, now shows B's first frame (an empty background here, black on a fade-in) instead of its picture.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a Save project file on another project from Home throws away the undo, playhead and selection of the project he has open — and repaints that card from its first frame. Fails at 1280 with a real mouse, in both passes: he was working in HUNTa7 Working on, went Home and used ⋯ → Save project file… on HUNTa7 Backup me. His own project, still open behind Home: Undo has nothing left to take back; the playhead is at 0.00 s instead of 1.20 s where he left it; the layer he had selected is no longer selected; and the HUNTa7 Backup me card now shows its first frame, an empty background, instead of the picture it had.
confirmed.evidence: js/home.js:1411 `const ok = await openProject(p.id, true);` loads B, js/home.js:1413 exports it, and js/home.js:1414 `if (prev && prev !== p.id) { await openProject(prev, true); render(); }` reloads A from disk. projects.open() then runs js/storage.js:2467 (`FM.time = 0`, selection cleared) and js/storage.js:2471 `FM.history.reset()`. On the switch back, js/storage.js:2441 `this.touchCurrent(true)` captures B's card at time 0 (js/storage.js:2400).
confirmed.fix: Do not switch projects to back up a card that is not open. Serialize B straight from its stored doc and IndexedDB media, the way packFromProject and templates.exportFile already do. If a switch cannot be avoided, keep and restore A's history, time and selection, and skip the thumbnail capture for a project that was only loaded in the background.

This is a real bug that Ezra would hit. I re-ran the test on port 9001 and it failed with all four symptoms: no undo left, playhead at 0.00 s instead of 1.20 s, the selected layer deselected, and B's card picture changed.

I then checked it by hand in a normal page at http://localhost:9001/index.html, with no test helpers and exportFile stubbed:
- **Going Home alone loses nothing.** Undo, the 1.2 s playhead and the selection are all still there on Home.
- **The loss comes only from ⋯ → Save project file… on another card.** After it, he is back in his own project (OPEN badge still on it) with undo empty, playhead 0 and nothing selected.
- **Going back in does not recover it.** Tapping his project's card closes Home with no reload, because that project is still the open one. He is in the editor with Undo greyed out; his last edit (x=220) is saved, but he cannot take it back.

Why it happens (js/home.js:1409-1415): the action opens B with openProject(p.id, true), exports it, then calls openProject(prev, true). At that point B is the open project, so needsLoad is true and FM.projects.open(prev) runs a full reload. That reload always sets FM.time = 0, clears the selection and calls FM.history.reset() (js/storage.js:2467-2471).

This goes against what the code says it means to do. The comment at home.js:1407 says the file "still exports without stealing the OPEN badge from your project", and the comment at history.js:224 says going back into the same project keeps the undo stack. Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for this behaviour. The only related entry (#385 clause 3) is about the same-project keepOpen path, where there is no reload.

The code path does not depend on screen width, so this happens on the phone too. The fake exportFile does not change anything, because the switch back runs whatever the export does.

The card-picture claim is real but minor. On the switch back, touchCurrent(true) redraws B's picture at time 0. That is what any open-and-leave of B already does, so he would only see a difference when B's first frame differs from its saved picture, such as a late clip or a fade-in.

Medium severity is about right. No project data is lost, but his undo history, playhead and selection are, from an action that looks like it only writes a backup file.

confirmed.title: Duplicate or Rename on a card down a long list moves the result to the top, off screen, with nothing saying where it went
confirmed.see: He scrolls down his list to an older project and taps ⋯ → Duplicate. A 'Duplicating…' toast flashes and nothing on screen changes: the copy was put first in the list, about 4,000 px above where he is looking. The natural next move is to press Duplicate again, which makes a second copy. Rename does the same: the card he just renamed disappears from where he was looking.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a Duplicate or Rename on a project down his long list sends the card to the top, off screen, and nothing says so — to him it did nothing. Fails at 380 and 900, with real taps: he scrolled down to HUNTa7 far 39 and pressed ⋯ → Duplicate. The copy, HUNTa7 far 39 copy, went to the top of the list, 4354 px above the screen he was looking at, and the only message was Duplicating…. Also, he renamed HUNTa7 far 45 to HUNTa7 far 45 final from its ⋯ and the card vanished from where he was looking.
confirmed.evidence: js/home.js:1346 Duplicate toasts only 'Duplicating…' and then render(). The copy is unshifted with modified = now at js/storage.js:2572, so it sorts first. js/home.js:1322 Rename calls FM.projects.rename, which sets `e.modified = Date.now()` (js/storage.js:2693), so the renamed card also sorts first. Neither action scrolls to the card or says where it went.
confirmed.fix: After Duplicate or Rename from a card's ⋯, bring the resulting card into view (scroll the list to it and give it a brief highlight), or say where it went ('Duplicated — it's at the top'). For Rename, keeping the card in place, or scrolling to its new spot, both avoid it vanishing.

This is real, but it is a missing-feedback problem, not broken data. Duplicate is clearly real; the Rename half is weaker.

I re-ran it on the hunt7-a worktree (port 9001, `?only=HUNT-a Duplicate or Rename`) and it fails the way the hunter said: the copy of "HUNTa7 far 39" landed 4354 px above the screen, and the renamed "far 45" card left the view.

It waits 1.5 s after the card appears, so this is not a timing trick.

- **Duplicate (`js/home.js` ~1346):** shows the toast "Duplicating…" (1200 ms), awaits `FM.projects.duplicate`, then calls `render()`. On success nothing else is said; the only other toast is the failure one. `duplicate` puts the copy first in the list with `modified = Date.now()` (`js/storage.js` ~2570). `render()` keeps the scroll position, so the copy appears far above him.
- **Bulk Select → Duplicate (`js/home.js` ~1627):** does end with "Duplicated N". The single-card ⋯ path is the only one that never confirms success.
- **Nothing brings the new card into view:** `js/home.js` has no `scrollIntoView` or highlight.

So what he sees is a "Duplicating…" flash with no copy in sight. That can lead him to tap Duplicate again and end up with a second copy.

Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for a silent duplicate. He only asked for the date/name sort (Settings → Project sorting) and pins (#138).

Rename is weaker. `rename()` pushes the card to the top on purpose; the comment says "renaming is a real change → bumps list order". That was Claude's choice, not his request. Under date sort it is consistent, but still confusing, because the card he just renamed leaves the screen with nothing saying where it went.

Severity medium is about right, maybe low-medium for Rename. None of this loses data; it is about feedback and where the card ends up.

verdict.reason:
This is real, but it is a missing-feedback problem, not broken data. Duplicate is clearly real; the Rename half is weaker.

I re-ran it on the hunt7-a worktree (port 9001, `?only=HUNT-a Duplicate or Rename`) and it fails the way the hunter said: the copy of "HUNTa7 far 39" landed 4354 px above the screen, and the renamed "far 45" card left the view.

The test is fair. It uses real CDP taps on the ⋯ menu, the menu item and the Rename OK button, all at phone width. Only the rename text is typed in by script, which does not matter here. The fixture is 62 seeded projects, but the same thing happens with any list long enough that its top is off screen, which at 380 px is only a handful of cards. It waits 1.5 s after the card appears, so this is not a timing trick.

What the code does:
- **Duplicate (`js/home.js` ~1346):** shows the toast "Duplicating…" (1200 ms), awaits `FM.projects.duplicate`, then calls `render()`. On success nothing else is said; the only other toast is the failure one. `duplicate` puts the copy first in the list with `modified = Date.now()` (`js/storage.js` ~2570). `render()` keeps the scroll position, so the copy appears far above him.
- **Bulk Select → Duplicate (`js/home.js` ~1627):** does end with "Duplicated N". The single-card ⋯ path is the only one that never confirms success.
- **Nothing brings the new card into view:** `js/home.js` has no `scrollIntoView` or highlight.

So what he sees is a "Duplicating…" flash with no copy in sight. That can lead him to tap Duplicate again and end up with a second copy.

Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for a silent duplicate. He only asked for the date/name sort (Settings → Project sorting) and pins (#138).

Rename is weaker. `rename()` pushes the card to the top on purpose; the comment says "renaming is a real change → bumps list order". That was Claude's choice, not his request. Under date sort it is consistent, but still confusing, because the card he just renamed leaves the screen with nothing saying where it went.

Severity medium is about right, maybe low-medium for Rename. None of this loses data; it is about feedback and where the card ends up.

confirmed.title: The exported file pops at the start and end of every trimmed clip. The preview fades each edge, so he never hears the pops while editing
confirmed.see: He trims a song so it starts or stops partway through the music, or cuts between two clips. In the preview the cut is smooth. In the exported video there is a sharp pop at every cut. This covers every trim, every change from one clip to another, and every song that stops before the video ends. Measured: a trimmed song goes from silence to full level (0.00 to 0.50) in one sample where it starts, and from 0.50 to 0.00 where it ends. That step is 31 times steeper than anything in the song itself. The preview plays the same edge at 2 percent 1 ms in.
confirmed.test: HUNT-b a trimmed song pops where it starts and where it ends in the exported file, while the preview fades each edge -- fails with: a song trimmed to play from 1.00 s to 2.50 s jumps from 0.00 to 0.50 in a single sample where it starts, and from 0.50 to 0.00 where it ends, in the exported soundtrack (31 times the steepest step of the song itself) - a pop at every cut in the file. The preview never plays these pops: it fades each clip edge over 45 ms (1 ms in, it plays at 2 percent; 1 ms before the end, at 2 percent). So every trim, every cut between two clips and every song that stops before the video does clicks in the exported video but not while he edits
confirmed.evidence: js/exporter.js:642 `gain.gain.value = vol;` (or the fade schedule just above it), then js/exporter.js:691 `node.connect(gain);` and js/exporter.js:694 `node.start(oStart - from, ..., oEnd - oStart)`. The clip's buffer starts on whatever sample the trim lands on and stops hard at oEnd, and nothing ramps either edge. The preview puts every clip edge through the 45 ms de-click: js/app.js:1851 `if (into < DECLICK_S && !seamAt(layer, layer.start)) k = Math.min(k, Math.max(0, into) / DECLICK_S);` and the matching `left < DECLICK_S` line, applied at js/app.js:2189 `const vol = lvl * declickGain(layer, FM.time, m, now);`. The seamAt comment in js/app.js already says the export does not build this envelope.
confirmed.fix: In buildAudioMix, give each clip the same edge envelope the preview uses: ramp 0 to 1 over DECLICK_S (45 ms) from the clip's own start, and 1 to 0 over DECLICK_S before its own end. Put it on a small per-clip GainNode between the node and the volume gain. Skip an edge that touches a split sibling, using the same seamAt rule so split halves stay continuous. Skip an edge the export range cuts through (oStart > layer.start or oEnd < clip end), because the clip is not really starting or ending there. A temporary 45 ms edge ramp made this test pass.

verdict.reason:
I ran the test on the worktree (port 9002) and it failed exactly as reported. The trimmed 250 Hz sine goes from 0.00 to 0.50 in one sample where the clip starts and from 0.50 to 0.00 where it ends. That step is 31 times the song's own steepest step. Both controls passed: mid-clip the level is 0.5, and the sample-to-sample steps inside the clip are normal.

I read the code and the pop comes from the app, not the test. In js/exporter.js buildAudioMix, each clip goes node -> gain -> (effects) -> destination. The gain is either `gain.gain.value = vol` or the user's own fade schedule, and fadeIn/fadeOut default to 0 (scene.js:698). `node.start(oStart - from, offset, oEnd - oStart)` starts the audio on whatever sample the trim lands on and stops it dead at the end. makeClipBuffer does not ramp the edges either, and nothing after the render softens them: the mix only gets a peak scan and a limiter. The preview does ramp every clip edge through declickGain over 45 ms (DECLICK_S, js/app.js:1827-1862, applied at app.js:2189). Ezra reported that popping in #148 and later confirmed the preview fix worked ("Seems fixed for the scratchy popping", #663). Nothing in REQUESTS.md says the export was meant to stay without the ramp. The seamAt comment in app.js even says the export "does not build the envelope this way" and calls the preview/render difference worse.

On the fixture: trimStart = 1.001 puts the cut on a crest to get the biggest step, so the 31x figure is a worst case. The effect itself is real, though. Any trim of real music lands mid-waveform, and a jump from silence to a typical music sample value in one sample is a textbook click. The same happens when a clip is cut shorter than its source or at a hard cut between two clips with sound. He can reach this with ordinary edits (trim a song, cut between phone clips) and export with default settings. He would hear pops in the exported file that he never hears while editing. One limit on the claim: an untrimmed clip whose source starts in silence will not pop at its start, so "every trim" and "every cut" should not be read as "every clip".

confirmed.title: Splitting a song leaves a short drop to near-silence at the cut in the preview. The export plays straight through
confirmed.see: He splits a song, for example to change the volume of one part or to cut it, and plays across the split. Every time the playhead crosses the cut, the sound drops to near-silence for about 45 ms and then fades back in. Measured at the speakers: the level falls to 0 percent right at the cut. The same song unsplit holds 98 percent there, and the exported file holds 97 percent. A split is meant to be inaudible, and the 21 Aug seam fix was supposed to guarantee that.
confirmed.test: HUNT-b splitting a song leaves a drop-out at the cut when he plays across it, while the export plays straight through -- fails with: he splits a song at 2.00 s and plays across the cut: the sound drops to 0 percent of its level right at the cut (at 2.01 s), a blip of near-silence every time the playhead crosses a split, where the same song unsplit holds 98 percent and the exported file holds 97 percent. The tail half opens silent and fades in over 45 ms because its element was paused until the cut (declickGain: the _resumedAt term, which the split seam exemption does not cover)
confirmed.evidence: js/app.js:1856 `if (m && m._resumedAt) {` has no seam check. The tail half's element stays paused until the playhead reaches it. Then the paused-to-play branch of syncMediaToClock sets `m.el.volume = 0` and js/app.js:2086 `m._resumedAt = now;`, so the half opens silent and ramps up over 45 ms. The seam exemption at js/app.js:1851 (`!seamAt(layer, layer.start)`) covers only the clip-relative term. The existing test 'split: the cut does not duck the sound to silence in preview' calls `FM._declickGain(l, t, null, 0)` with m = null, so it never exercises the _resumedAt term.
confirmed.fix: In declickGain, skip the _resumedAt ramp when the element is being opened at a split seam (into near 0 and seamAt(layer, layer.start)). Then also pre-roll the tail half so it is already playing when the playhead arrives: seek it to its first frame and start it silent a few hundred ms before its start, the same way FM.play waits for sound. Otherwise element start-up latency, which is larger on a phone, leaves a gap. The seam exemption alone made this test pass in Chrome.

verdict.reason:
I re-ran the test on the worktree served at port 9002 and it failed the same way. The split song dropped to 0 percent at 2.02 s. The unsplit control held 98 percent in the same window and the exported mix held 97 percent. Both controls passed, so the speaker tap was working and the dip is caused by the split.

The code path matches the report:
- splitLayer (js/app.js:4886 reloadMediaTo) gives the tail half its own media element.
- syncMediaToClock pauses that element while layerLocalTime is null, which is every moment before the cut. No pre-roll logic exists anywhere.
- When the playhead reaches 2.00 s, the paused-element branch (js/app.js:2084-2090) sets el.volume = 0 and m._resumedAt = now, then seeks and calls play().
- The volume reconcile (line ~2190: vol = lvl * declickGain(layer, FM.time, m, now)) then ramps the half up over 45 ms from that time.
- The seam exemption (lines 1851-1852) covers only the two clip-edge terms. The _resumedAt term at line 1856 has no seamAt check. On top of the ramp, the element takes time to start after play().

I checked for test artefacts:
- The 0 dB Gain effect only puts the element through Web Audio so the tap can hear it. The chain is built for all layers at FM.play() (syncAll at line 2340), so nothing is being set up at the cut. Without an effect the same ramp still goes to el.volume, so he would hear it either way.
- The existing test 'split: the cut does not duck the sound to silence in preview' (tests.js:10337) calls FM._declickGain(l, t, null, 0) with m = null, so it never exercises the _resumedAt term.
- Nothing in REQUESTS.md makes a gap at a split intended. The 21 Aug seam fix and the fade-splitting comments both say a split is meant to be inaudible.

The steps are split a song, then play across the cut, which is ordinary editing. He would hear a short near-silent blip in the preview every time the playhead crosses a split, while the file plays straight through. Medium severity fits. The hunter is also right that exempting seams in declickGain is not enough on its own. The tail element still starts late, and that delay is likely longer on a phone, so the tail half needs to be started early.

confirmed.title: The exported video's sound is 44 ms behind the picture, and the audio track runs 72 ms past the end of the video
confirmed.see: Every exported video with sound plays its soundtrack 44 ms after the picture. A click at 1.000 s on his timeline is at 1.044 s in the exported MP4, and a 3.000 s video has a 3.072 s audio track. Speech is at the edge of visible lip-sync error, and cuts timed to the beat land late. If he exports a clip and imports it into another project, it slips another 44 ms each time.
confirmed.test: HUNT-b the sound in an exported video comes 44 ms after the picture -- fails with: a click at 1.000 s on his timeline is at 1.044 s in the exported MP4: the whole soundtrack plays 44 ms behind the picture in every exported video (and the audio track is 3.072 s long for a 3.000 s video). The AAC encoder starts every stream with a warm-up it does not mean to be heard, and the file carries no edit list telling a player to skip it, so every player plays it. Speech sits at the edge of visible lip-sync error, cuts on the beat land late, and a clip he exports and imports again drifts another 44 ms each time
confirmed.evidence: js/exporter.js:821 `enc.configure({ codec: 'mp4a.40.2', sampleRate, numberOfChannels: channels, bitrate: 160000 });` and js/exporter.js:832 feed AudioData from `timestamp: Math.round(ts)` starting at 0. Every output chunk goes to the muxer unchanged, starting with the encoder's 2112 priming samples. js/exporter.js:1243-1247 builds `new Mp4Muxer.Muxer({ ... audio: { codec: 'aac', ... }, fastStart: false })`. vendor/mp4-muxer.js writes no edts, elst or sgpd box (grep count 0), so nothing tells a player to skip the priming. The test's control shows the soundtrack buildAudioMix produces has the click at exactly 1.000 s, so the 44 ms is added by the encode and mux.
confirmed.fix: Remove the priming before muxing. Drop the encoder's first two 1024-sample output chunks and shift the rest back by the first kept chunk's timestamp. That leaves 64 samples (1.3 ms) of warm-up, and the decoderConfig meta must be passed with the first kept chunk. The alternative is to write an edit list, but this muxer cannot. Apply the same fix in encodeM4A, the audio-only export. Also stop the audio track at the video's length. A temporary drop-two-chunks version made this test pass.

verdict.reason:
I re-ran the test against the worktree, which is already being served on port 9002 from hunt7-b. It fails as reported: the click sits at exactly 1.000 s in the soundtrack buildAudioMix makes, and at 1.044 s in the exported MP4 after decoding it. The audio track is 3.072 s long. 44 ms is exactly 2112 samples at 48 kHz, the standard AAC-LC encoder warm-up, and 3.072 s is 144 frames of 1024 samples. Both numbers point at encoder warm-up, not the mix.

The code path matches the report:
- js/exporter.js encodeAudio (lines 810-839) feeds AudioData from timestamp 0 and passes every output chunk through unchanged, warm-up chunks included.
- The muxer uses firstTimestampBehavior "strict", so the first chunk sits at 0.
- vendor/mp4-muxer.js has no edts or elst box at all (grep count 0), so the file never tells a player to skip the warm-up.

Without an edit list (or iTunSMPB), players go by the sample table and play every sample. That covers Chrome/FFmpeg-based players, and most likely AVFoundation too. So this is a real property of the file, not something the fixture, a synthetic event or the timing produced. Nothing in REQUESTS.md or POLISH-LOG.md asks for it or explains it away.

Caveats on how bad it is:
- A 44 ms audio lag is at the ATSC limit (45 ms) and inside EBU R37 (60 ms lag). It is below the ITU-R BT.1359 point where people notice a lag (about 125 ms). So "at the edge of visible lip-sync error" is a little strong for one export.
- The user-facing effects that hold up: the file does not match his timeline, beat-timed cuts are off by about 1.3 frames at 30 fps, and it adds up when an export is imported back in (the import decodes the warm-up as real sound). The audio track also runs 72 ms past the video.
- I only confirmed it in Chrome on Mac. I could not test Safari on iPhone (the browser pane refused localhost), though its AAC encoder also has warm-up, so the same result is likely.
- The suggested fix of dropping chunks leaves a small artefact in the first ~21 ms where the decoder lacks overlap. That is a detail of the fix and does not change the verdict.

Nothing was edited.

confirmed.title: On an iPhone, a clip with Echo or Reverb that is not at 100 percent volume, or has a fade, goes silent the moment it ends in the preview. In the export the echo keeps ringing
confirmed.see: On his phone he puts Echo or Reverb on a voice clip and turns it down (for example 80 percent) or gives it a fade. While he previews, the echo or reverb stops dead the moment the clip ends. In the exported video it rings on after the clip. Measured: after the clip ends, the phone preview's echo is 1 percent of the clip's level. The exported file has 44 percent, and the same clip at 100 percent has 52 percent in the preview. The order problem also means effects like Distortion, Compressor and Limiter process the clip at full level on the phone but at its real level in the file. So what he mixes by ear on the phone is not what the file contains.
confirmed.test: HUNT-b on an iPhone a clip with Echo that is not at 100 percent stops dead at its end in the preview, but the echo rings on in the export -- fails with: on his iPhone, a voice clip at 80 percent with Echo goes silent the moment the clip ends in the preview - the echo after it measured 1 percent of the clip, where the exported file rings on at 44 percent and the same clip at 100 percent rings on at 52 percent in the preview. The level stage an iPhone needs sits AFTER the effects, so the end-of-clip fade silences the echo and reverb tails too; the export turns the clip down BEFORE the effects. Any volume but 100 percent, or any fade, does it - so what he hears on the phone is not what the file contains
confirmed.evidence: js/audio-fx-live.js:252 `const boost = needsBoost(layer) ? makeBoostStage(ctx) : (needsLevel(layer, m) ? makeLevelStage(ctx) : null);`, then js/audio-fx-live.js:254 `const tail = boost ? boost.input : ctx.destination;` and js/audio-fx-live.js:263-264 `mes.connect(chain.input); chain.output.connect(tail);`. The routing is element, then effects, then level stage, then speakers. The playback tick drives that stage with volume, fade and de-click (js/app.js:2189 `const vol = lvl * declickGain(...)` and js/app.js:2229 `FM.audioFxLive.setBoost(layer, vol);`). At the clip's end the stage goes to about 0 and silences the echo tail that sits upstream of it. The export applies volume and fade first: js/exporter.js:691 `node.connect(gain);` then js/exporter.js:656 `gain.connect(chain.input);`. The test copies the HUNT-e WebKit stand-in: el.volume reads 1 and ignores writes.
confirmed.fix: In audioFxLive.sync, when the stage is a level stage (makeLevelStage, meaning needsLevel and not boosted), wire it before the effects: mes, then level, then chain, then destination. That matches the export's order and the desktop's upstream el.volume. Keep the boost stage and its limiter last. Rebuilding with that wiring made this test pass. Check that the reversed-clip path in audio-play.js is unaffected; it already puts the volume gain before its chain.

verdict.reason:
REAL, and he would hit it on his iPhone. I re-ran the test in the worktree and it fails the same way. The 80 percent clip's echo after the clip ended measured 8 percent of the clip. The hunter reported 1 percent, but either way it is far under the 20 percent threshold. The controls passed on the same run: the same clip at 100 percent with no level stage rang on at 51 percent in the preview, and the exported 80 percent clip rang on at 44 percent. So the tap does hear a tail and the file does contain one.

Code path, checked in the worktree:
- js/audio-fx-live.js sync() wires element -> MediaElementSource -> effects chain -> level/boost stage -> speakers (lines 252-265). On an iPhone, a clip that is not a flat 100 percent (any volume change or any fade) gets makeLevelStage, because volumeLocked() finds that el.volume will not keep a value.
- The playback tick in js/app.js sets vol = layerVolume x fadeMul x declickGain and calls setBoost(layer, vol) on every tick. On a locked element setBoost floors at 0, so over the last 45 ms the de-click (and any fade-out) drives that gain to about 0.
- Once the playhead leaves the clip (local == null), the tick pauses and mutes the element and returns without writing setBoost again. The stage stays frozen near 0, and because the Delay/Reverb nodes sit upstream of it, their tail is cut.
- On desktop, el.volume is upstream of the source node, so the tail rings. The export (js/exporter.js 644-691: node -> gain -> chain -> destination) and the reversed path in audio-play.js both put the level before the effects, so the tail rings there too.
- The iPhone forward path is the only one with the reverse order. That also means Distortion, Compressor and Limiter process the clip at full level on the phone.

The WebKit stand-in (el.volume reads 1 and ignores writes) matches Apple's documented iOS behaviour and the app's own volumeLocked detection, so the fixture is fair. It uses no synthetic input, and the timing is loose (tail window 1.1-1.45 s against a 1.0 s clip end). Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for tails to stop at the clip end. The comment in sync() about putting the stage last is about the boost's limiter; the level stage (queue 690) just reused that slot. Severity medium: it only affects iPhone preview, clips with Echo/Reverb (or level-sensitive effects) and a volume other than 100 percent or a fade, but on his main device the mix he hears differs from the file.

Two notes for the fixer:
1. The test cannot merge as written. The hunter's new `async function huntBTap()` (tests.js:98823) has the same name as the existing `function huntBTap(x, y)` (tests.js:88373), and both are in the same top-level IIFE. verdict.reason:

It fails as reported: the click sits at exactly 1.000 s in the soundtrack buildAudioMix makes, and at 1.044 s in the exported MP4 after decoding it. The audio track is 3.072 s long. 44 ms is exactly 2112 samples at 48 kHz, the standard AAC-LC encoder warm-up, and 3.072 s is 144 frames of 1024 samples. - js/exporter.js encodeAudio (lines 810-839) feeds AudioData from timestamp 0 and passes every output chunk through unchanged, warm-up chunks included.

- A 44 ms audio lag is at the ATSC limit (45 ms) and inside EBU R37 (60 ms lag). It is below the ITU-R BT.1359 point where people notice a lag (about 125 ms). So "at the edge of visible lip-sync error" is a little strong for one export.

confirmed.title: When he opens the app with no signal, it says the app looks old and tells him to tap the version chip. Tapping the chip with no network deletes the offline copy, and the installed app shows an error page until signal returns
confirmed.see: He opens FreeMotion on a train, or on Wi-Fi that does not reach the internet. The app opens from its offline copy, as it should. About a second later it shows this message: Your connection dropped on refresh, so FreeMotion loaded v17.00 from its offline copy — that is why it looks old. Tap the version chip to get the latest. Nothing is old: v17.00 is the build he has. It shows on every launch with no signal. He does what it says and taps the chip. The screen becomes the browser's 'This site can't be reached' page. Closing and reopening the app shows the same error page until he has signal again. The message is also the #306 diagnostic he was asked to watch for ('if you see it, this was the cause'), so every offline launch would wrongly confirm that the service worker caused the old-build glitch. I checked this end to end in headless Chrome against a real server before writing the test. I installed the app and let it cache, stopped the server, and relaunched. The app opened offline and showed exactly that message. I tapped the chip and the page went to chrome-error://chromewebdata/. The next launch showed 'refused to connect'. navigator.onLine was still true throughout, which is his phone on a connection that does not reach the internet.

Tap the version chip to get the latest. — so he taps the version chip while offline; no signal at all, the copy it calls old is v17.00, the build that is running — nothing is old, the network is just down; no signal at all, a tap on the chip went straight on to unregister the offline worker without finding out whether the new build could be fetched — the page then navigates to an address that cannot load, and with the worker and its cache gone the installed app shows a browser error page on every launch until the network is back; (the same three again for a network that does not reach the internet, navigator.onLine still true).
confirmed.evidence: sw.js:165-173: any navigation whose fetch throws twice is answered from 'index-fallback' and stamped with `c.put(STALE_KEY, new Response(m ? m[1] : '?'))`. A launch with no signal is exactly that case, and the fallback is the last good load, which is normally this same build. index.html:1157: `setTimeout(... FM.checkStaleShell() ..., 1500)`. js/app.js:1264 and 1274: FM.staleShellNotice always says 'that is why it looks old. Tap the version chip to get the latest.' verdict.reason:
This is a real problem. I ran the test with ?only=HUNT-d%20opened%20with%20no%20signal on port 9004 and it failed with exactly the reported message. That held in both passes: navigator.onLine false, and navigator.onLine true with every fetch failing. The test's own control checks passed first, so it was measuring the real thing.

The code path:
- Opening with no signal is a supported feature. #112 in REQUESTS.md was built and tested so the app opens on a train.
- On that launch, sw.js lines 146-175 try the page fetch twice. When both fail, sw.js serves 'index-fallback' and stamps 'served-stale-shell' with the version of that copy.
- index-fallback is overwritten on every good load, so it is normally the build he is already running.
- 1.5 s after load, index.html line 1157 calls FM.checkStaleShell. That shows FM.staleShellNotice (js/app.js 1261-1265), which always says the app 'looks old' and to 'Tap the version chip to get the latest'.
- Nothing checks whether the network is back or whether a newer build exists. So every launch with no signal shows that false message.
- The chip handler (index.html 1166-1178) unregisters every service worker and deletes every cache, then calls location.replace to a new ?fresh= address. It never checks that the new build can be fetched first.
- With no network that address cannot load. Even a worker that was still attached would find its cache empty and answer with an error page.
- The worker only registers again from a page that loads (on the 'load' event), so every launch after that is a browser error page until signal returns.

So the app's own message sends him to the one tap that removes its offline copy. The test is not an artefact:
- The chip test uses a real, trusted mouse click.
- The stand-ins only record the unregister and cache calls and stop the reload. They do not change which path the code takes.
- The worker half runs the real sw.js.

No request asks for the chip to wipe the offline copy with no signal. Its stated purpose is getting the latest build, which is impossible offline. #306 designed the message for a brief dropout on refresh, not a launch with no signal at all. It is closed ('I think it's fine'), so the claim that the message would wrongly confirm that diagnosis now matters less.

Severity is lower than 'high' in one way: no project data is lost. The only Cache Storage the app uses is the app-shell cache 'freemotion-v1'; projects live in localStorage and IndexedDB. The app comes back once he has signal. But the false 'looks old' message on every offline launch, followed by the app becoming unusable offline because he followed it, is a user-facing defect he would hit on any launch without signal.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug. I re-ran the test on port 9004, where a server was already serving the hunt7-d worktree, and it failed with the same message the hunter reported.

**The test is sound.**
- Its checks pass before it asserts anything: the full store really refuses the save (flushSync returns false), and the app itself says the work is unsaved (unsavedOnScreen() is true).
- The click that reaches the label is a trusted mouse click.
- It only makes the store refuse the project's own key. A really full phone refuses every write, which is worse, not better.

**The code does what the report says.** In index.html around lines 1162-1180, the version-label click handler calls `FM.storage.flushSync()` and ignores the result. It then goes straight on to unregister the service worker, delete the caches and call `location.replace(...?fresh=)`.

**Nothing else saves the work.** There is no fallback copy of the project anywhere when the normal save is refused: I checked `writeScene` and `_writeFail` in js/storage.js, and nothing uses sessionStorage. There is also no `beforeunload` or `pagehide` handler that asks. After the reload, `load()` brings back the last saved copy, so everything since the "Storage full — autosave paused" toast is lost with no question asked.

**The other ways out of a project already ask, so this is inconsistent.** Opening another project and New project call `askLeave` (js/storage.js:2440 and 2479), Home's card tap goes through `confirmLeave` (js/storage.js:2302), and so does js/storage.js:1876. Stay is the default on all of them. The version label is the only door left that skips the question.

**He would really hit this.**
- A full phone is reachable: `warnQuota` exists because of #15, and every project is saved in the phone's local storage, which has a small size limit.
- REQUESTS.md shows he is often told to tap the version label to get the latest build (for example around line 32974), and the label's own tooltip says the same.
- Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for the label to reload without a question. Asking Stay / Leave anyway still lets him force the update.

The hunter's fix fits the existing pattern. Before anything is unregistered, check `FM.projects.confirmLeave()`; if he picks Stay, put the label back and stop.

On severity: running out of storage is uncommon, so "high" may be a little strong. When it does happen, though, it silently throws away real work.

verdict.reason:
This is a real defect that Ezra could hit. I ran the test and it failed with the reported message: after the round trip through Home the canvas shows red (IMG_3001.PNG), drawn 540 px wide where it had been 1080.

Port 9004 was already being served from this same worktree by PID 35086, so my serve.sh call could not bind. I ran the test against that server, after checking that it serves the hunt7-d directory and that its tests.js contains this test. I did not edit anything.

**The test setup matches a real full phone.** The test makes `IDBObjectStore.put` throw straight away for the layer's key. On a real phone the write fails later instead, when the transaction aborts with QuotaExceededError. Both routes end at the same place in `idbPut` (js/storage.js:295): `warnStore` then `res(false)`. So the save loop (js/storage.js:779-785) never counts the new file as saved, and `strikePending` leaves `_stored` at rev 0, the old file. The test also checks that the old red file is still what storage holds, and that the "Not enough storage to save that media" toast fired.

**How the code gets there:**
1. Replace media (js/app.js, `FM.replaceMedia`) keeps the old file under `prev:<id>:0`.
2. It swaps in the new file and bumps `layer.mediaRev` and the record's `rev` to 1.
3. `fitReplacedMedia` sets the layer's scale to fit the new file: 0.5 for 1080 wide to 4K.
4. It then saves, and the store refuses the new file.
5. Going Home runs `captureThumbSoon`, which calls `releaseSceneMedia` (js/home.js:419).
6. `releaseSceneMedia` only checks that some record exists under the layer's id: `if (!keys.has(id)) continue;` at js/storage.js:534. The old file is still there under that id, so the check passes and `FM.media.remove(id)` frees the only copy of the new file. That breaks the promise in the queue 385 comment: "NOTHING IS FREED THAT IDB CANNOT GIVE BACK".
7. Opening the project again, `_hydrateSceneMedia` (onlyMissing) reads the old rev-0 record and never compares it with `layer.mediaRev`. `reportPending` counts the layer as found, so nothing is said.

**Why it counts.** The old photo comes back at the new photo's scale, and the replace is silently undone within one session. Nothing in REQUESTS.md says media that could not be saved should be dropped on a trip Home. The v16.94 hunt-f fix treats a refused clip as something that plays from memory, now with a warning, so losing it after the warning is not intended behaviour. A full phone is a situation Ezra has run into before (REQUESTS.md has entries around lines 32544 and 32924). Replace media is in the ⋯ menu, and going Home and back is everyday use.

Severity medium is fair, since it needs storage to be full. The hunter's suggested fix fits the cause: only free a record when `_stored` says the in-memory revision is the one on disk.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug. I re-ran the test on port 9004 and it failed exactly as reported. The toasts, in order, were 'Storage full — autosave paused…' and then 'That project is no longer on this device'. Afterwards Home had closed into the editor, which still showed 'HUNT-d holiday edit', not the new 'Project 3'.

At line 2516 it calls open(id, {confirmed:true}). open() finds no index entry and no document, so at line 2428 it shows the 'no longer on this device' message and returns false before tearing anything down. create() ignores that false and returns the id anyway. In js/home.js, createFromDialog only stops on a falsy id, so it calls FM.home.close({push:true}) into the old project, which is still loaded.

Project documents live only in localStorage (fm.proj.*, about 5 MB per origin), and the app already has a 'Storage full' message for this state. The codebase also treats it as reachable elsewhere: duplicate() and the other copy path (lines 2561/2573 and 2623/2643) check both writes and remove the half-written document on failure, citing 'on a nearly-full phone the doc write failed' (queue 915). create() is the path that missed that fix.

That held in both passes: navigator.onLine false, and navigator.onLine true with every fetch failing. The test's own control checks passed first, so it was measuring the real thing.

The code path:
- Opening with no signal is a supported feature. #112 in REQUESTS.md was built and tested so the app opens on a train.
- On that launch, sw.js lines 146-175 try the page fetch twice. When both fail, sw.js serves 'index-fallback' and stamps 'served-stale-shell' with the version of that copy.
- index-fallback is overwritten on every good load, so it is normally the build he is already running.
- 1.5 s after load, index.html line 1157 calls FM.checkStaleShell. That shows FM.staleShellNotice (js/app.js 1261-1265), which always says the app 'looks old' and to 'Tap the version chip to get the latest'.
- Nothing checks whether the network is back or whether a newer build exists. So every launch with no signal shows that false message.
- The chip handler (index.html 1166-1178) unregisters every service worker and deletes every cache, then calls location.replace to a new ?fresh= address. It never checks that the new build can be fetched first.
- With no network that address cannot load. Even a worker that was still attached would find its cache empty and answer with an error page.
- The worker only registers again from a page that loads (on the 'load' event), so every launch after that is a browser error page until signal returns.

So the app's own message sends him to the one tap that removes its offline copy. The test is not an artefact:
- The chip test uses a real, trusted mouse click.
- The stand-ins only record the unregister and cache calls and stop the reload. They do not change which path the code takes.
- The worker half runs the real sw.js.

No request asks for the chip to wipe the offline copy with no signal. Its stated purpose is getting the latest build, which is impossible offline. #306 designed the message for a brief dropout on refresh, not a launch with no signal at all. It is closed ('I think it's fine'), so the claim that the message would wrongly confirm that diagnosis now matters less.

Severity is lower than 'high' in one way: no project data is lost. The only Cache Storage the app uses is the app-shell cache 'freemotion-v1'; projects live in localStorage and IndexedDB. The app comes back once he has signal. But the false 'looks old' message on every offline launch, followed by the app becoming unusable offline because he followed it, is a user-facing defect he would hit on any launch without signal.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug. I re-ran the test on port 9004, where a server was already serving the hunt7-d worktree, and it failed with the same message the hunter reported.

**The test is sound.**
- Its checks pass before it asserts anything: the full store really refuses the save (flushSync returns false), and the app itself says the work is unsaved (unsavedOnScreen() is true).
- The click that reaches the label is a trusted mouse click.
- It only makes the store refuse the project's own key. A really full phone refuses every write, which is worse, not better.

**The code does what the report says.** In index.html around lines 1162-1180, the version-label click handler calls `FM.storage.flushSync()` and ignores the result. It then goes straight on to unregister the service worker, delete the caches and call `location.replace(...?fresh=)`.

**Nothing else saves the work.** There is no fallback copy of the project anywhere when the normal save is refused: I checked `writeScene` and `_writeFail` in js/storage.js, and nothing uses sessionStorage. There is also no `beforeunload` or `pagehide` handler that asks. After the reload, `load()` brings back the last saved copy, so everything since the "Storage full — autosave paused" toast is lost with no question asked.

**The other ways out of a project already ask, so this is inconsistent.** Opening another project and New project call `askLeave` (js/storage.js:2440 and 2479), Home's card tap goes through `confirmLeave` (js/storage.js:2302), and so does js/storage.js:1876. Stay is the default on all of them. The version label is the only door left that skips the question.

**He would really hit this.**
- A full phone is reachable: `warnQuota` exists because of #15, and every project is saved in the phone's local storage, which has a small size limit.
- REQUESTS.md shows he is often told to tap the version label to get the latest build (for example around line 32974), and the label's own tooltip says the same.
- Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for the label to reload without a question. Asking Stay / Leave anyway still lets him force the update.

The hunter's fix fits the existing pattern. Before anything is unregistered, check `FM.projects.confirmLeave()`; if he picks Stay, put the label back and stop.

On severity: running out of storage is uncommon, so "high" may be a little strong. When it does happen, though, it silently throws away real work.

verdict.reason:
This is a real defect that Ezra could hit. I ran the test and it failed with the reported message: after the round trip through Home the canvas shows red (IMG_3001.PNG), drawn 540 px wide where it had been 1080.

Port 9004 was already being served from this same worktree by PID 35086, so my serve.sh call could not bind. I ran the test against that server, after checking that it serves the hunt7-d directory and that its tests.js contains this test. I did not edit anything.

**The test setup matches a real full phone.** The test makes `IDBObjectStore.put` throw straight away for the layer's key. On a real phone the write fails later instead, when the transaction aborts with QuotaExceededError. Both routes end at the same place in `idbPut` (js/storage.js:295): `warnStore` then `res(false)`. So the save loop (js/storage.js:779-785) never counts the new file as saved, and `strikePending` leaves `_stored` at rev 0, the old file. The test also checks that the old red file is still what storage holds, and that the "Not enough storage to save that media" toast fired.

**How the code gets there:**
1. Replace media (js/app.js, `FM.replaceMedia`) keeps the old file under `prev:<id>:0`.
2. It swaps in the new file and bumps `layer.mediaRev` and the record's `rev` to 1.
3. `fitReplacedMedia` sets the layer's scale to fit the new file: 0.5 for 1080 wide to 4K.
4. It then saves, and the store refuses the new file.
5. Going Home runs `captureThumbSoon`, which calls `releaseSceneMedia` (js/home.js:419).
6. `releaseSceneMedia` only checks that some record exists under the layer's id: `if (!keys.has(id)) continue;` at js/storage.js:534. The old file is still there under that id, so the check passes and `FM.media.remove(id)` frees the only copy of the new file. That breaks the promise in the queue 385 comment: "NOTHING IS FREED THAT IDB CANNOT GIVE BACK".
7. Opening the project again, `_hydrateSceneMedia` (onlyMissing) reads the old rev-0 record and never compares it with `layer.mediaRev`. `reportPending` counts the layer as found, so nothing is said.

**Why it counts.** The old photo comes back at the new photo's scale, and the replace is silently undone within one session. Nothing in REQUESTS.md says media that could not be saved should be dropped on a trip Home. The v16.94 hunt-f fix treats a refused clip as something that plays from memory, now with a warning, so losing it after the warning is not intended behaviour. A full phone is a situation Ezra has run into before (REQUESTS.md has entries around lines 32544 and 32924). Replace media is in the ⋯ menu, and going Home and back is everyday use.

Severity medium is fair, since it needs storage to be full. The hunter's suggested fix fits the cause: only free a record when `_stored` says the in-memory revision is the one on disk.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug. I re-ran the test on port 9004 and it failed exactly as reported. The toasts, in order, were 'Storage full — autosave paused…' and then 'That project is no longer on this device'. Afterwards Home had closed into the editor, which still showed 'HUNT-d holiday edit', not the new 'Project 3'.

The code confirms it. In js/storage.js, create() writes the new document at line 2502 and the index at line 2515 without checking whether either write worked (writeJSON returns false on a quota error). At line 2516 it calls open(id, {confirmed:true}). open() finds no index entry and no document, so at line 2428 it shows the 'no longer on this device' message and returns false before tearing anything down. create() ignores that false and returns the id anyway. In js/home.js, createFromDialog only stops on a falsy id, so it calls FM.home.close({push:true}) into the old project, which is still loaded.

The test fixture is fair. It refuses any localStorage write that adds a key or makes one bigger, which is how a full store behaves. Project documents live only in localStorage (fm.proj.*, about 5 MB per origin), and the app already has a 'Storage full' message for this state. The codebase also treats it as reachable elsewhere: duplicate() and the other copy path (lines 2561/2573 and 2623/2643) check both writes and remove the half-written document on failure, citing 'on a nearly-full phone the doc write failed' (queue 915). create() is the path that missed that fix.

The synthetic tap does not matter here. The defect is in create()'s logic, and a real finger reaches the same createFromDialog call. It is not intended behaviour: the message is false (the project was never made because there was no room) and he lands in the wrong project.

Related, not tested: the Elements 'Build a new one…' route (js/home.js:2156-2160) has the same problem. After a silent create failure it would set the OLD project's background to transparent and save it.

I edited nothing. I stopped the port-9004 server when I was done.
